title: Reliability stewardship campaign roadmap — tribal routes and sprint playbook
content:
Executive summary:

This is a tactical campaign-level plan to operationalize our reliability program for 2026, focused on SLO stewardship across product teams (hosted API, dedicated, private), platform, and SRE. The goal is to move beyond one-off SLOs toward a repeatable, cross-functional cadence that embeds runbook ownership, signal clarity, and lightweight gates for rollouts.

Why this exists:
- We continue to see model-serving incidents where the oncall and product teams disagree on signal meaning (is this a model drift problem, infra capacity, or a rollout bug?).
- Teams lack a common SLO lifecycle: design -> simulate -> gate -> monitor -> iterate.
- We need a campaign to build tribal knowledge (playbook fragments) and a repeatable sprint pattern to onboard teams.

Objectives (measurable):
1) Onboard 8 feature teams to the SLO stewardship process by end of Q2 2026 (target: each team has a documented SLO, runbook, and one tabletop).
2) Reduce P99 user-visible latency incidents caused by rollout regressions by 35% over 6 months.
3) Create a single canonical SLO design template and automated checklist consumed by CI gating (GH action) for canary rollouts.

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In-scope: SLO design templates, cross-team tabletop schedule, runbook templates, CI gating checklist, basic dashboards and alerts, two-week trial with hosted-api and one dedicated customer flow.
- Out-of-scope: full observability rewrite, long-term billing/cost signals, deep model-eval tooling (those stay with Optimize/RnD as separate projects).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Campaign lead: Asha Menon (eng-site-reliability) — overall deliverables and stakeholder coordination.
- Product partners: Lina Rodriguez (product-hosted-api), Tomáš Novák (product-dedicated).
- SRE liaison: Ethan Cole — runbook and oncall integration.
- DevEx: Priya Kapoor — templates, docs, and developer onboarding.
- Executive sponsor: VP Infrastructure (TBD).

Tribal routes (cross-functional paths):
We will create three repeatable "tribal routes" (short playbooks) teams can follow depending on service criticality:
1) Green route (low-impact): single SLO, lightweight runbook, ramp in 2 sprints.
2) Amber route (medium-impact): multiple SLOs (latency + error rate), canary gating in CI, weekly mini-tabletop during rollout.
3) Red route (customer-impacting): full onboarding, A/B gating, dedicated stability buddy, daily health checks for 2 weeks post-launch.

Sprint plan (12-week campaign broken into 6 x 2-week sprints):
Sprint 0 (prep, week -2 to 0): finalize templates, define signals we care about (latency histograms, error taxonomy), create first dashboards (generic service SLO).
Sprint 1: Pilot with hosted-api internal feature team (green -> amber path): co-design SLO, create runbook, run 1 tabletop.
Sprint 2: Integrate CI gating checklist for canaries (GH action), wire basic alert routing to SRE Slack channel, iterate pilot.
Sprint 3: Onboard dedicated product team pilot (amber -> red path), perform simulated traffic tabletop that includes cross-region fallback.
Sprint 4: Run cross-functional simulation (platform, infra, product, SRE) that intentionally triggers fallback to model-variant; capture decisions, update playbook.
Sprint 5: Campaign close, knowledge transfer, create handoff package for long-term stewardship and roadmap for next quarter.

Deliverables by sprint:
- Templates: SLO design (metrics, measurement windows), runbook stub, postmortem checklist.
- Automation: GH action for gating, monitoring dashboard template, alert routing playbook.
- Trainings: 30–60 min brown bags per pilot team, tabletop scripts.

Communication and cadence:
- Weekly 30 min campaign sync (Wednesdays) — standing invite to product leads, SRE liaisons, devex.
- Bi-weekly notes posted to Confluence campaign page and Slack #reliability-campaign channel.
- Quick escalation path: page SRE duty + campaign lead if a pilot shows repeatable signal mismatch.

KPIs and signals to monitor:
- Adoption: number of teams with SLO + runbook in Confluence (target 8 by end Q2).
- Safety: percent of rollouts using CI gating (target 60% for pilot teams).
- Outcome: P99 user latency incidents attributable to rollout/regression (baseline and drop target).
- Process: mean time to update runbook after tabletop (target < 5 days).

Runbook & playbook examples (fragments):
- Incident triage steps: (1) confirm signal source (app infra / model / data), (2) check feature flags & canary cohorts, (3) fallback to stable model variant, (4) page SRE and owner.
- Post-deploy checks (first 30 minutes): traffic ratios, error rate vs baseline, cost spike monitor.

Gating and rollout criteria (minimum):
- Canary must show no more than +10% error rate and +5% P99 over baseline for 10k requests.
- If canary violates thresholds, auto-fallback and blocking PR for rollout.

Training & onboarding plan:
- Two-hour onboarding workshop (hands-on): SLO template walkthrough, runbook authoring, simulating a canary fail using a local workload generator.
- Playback: record sessions and publish to campaign Confluence.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: teams view this as extra overhead. Mitigation: provide pre-filled templates and a one-click GH action to reduce friction.
- Risk: alert fatigue. Mitigation: tune alerts for SLO burn rate and only page on burn rate > threshold.
- Risk: ownership ambiguity. Mitigation: require documented owner in SLO template and product sign-off before gate removal.

Budget and resourcing ask (high-level):
- 0.3 FTE SRE for 12 weeks (triage, tabletop facilitation).
- 0.2 FTE DevEx for templates and automation.
- Minimal infra sandbox cost (estimate $2k for synthetic load and short-lived clusters).

Next actions (first 2 weeks):
- Finalize templates (Asha, Priya) — due 2025-11-20.
- Schedule hosted-api pilot kickoff with Lina — due 2025-11-24.
- Create GH action stub and dashboard starter — assigned to Tomáš.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Which VP will sponsor this long-term? Need OKR alignment.
- Ask Legal about sharing tabletop outcomes externally (customer-facing).
- Consider short experiment to surface model-quality signals into SLOs (coordinate with Applied ML).

Appendix (quick links and references):
- Example incident: GH:repo/incidents/982 (rollout caused P99 spike, mismatched alert filters).
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/internal/reliability-stewardship-campaign
- Tickets: ENG-1123 (campaign plan), ENG-1209 (CI gating), OBS-88 (dashboard templates).

Notes: this doc is intentionally conversational — will convert to a one-pager and a checklist once pilots confirm the route templates.
